stem: Which radiographic view is most likely to reveal a mild slipped capital femoral epiphysis?
explanation: Frog lateral view is the best view for detecting a mild slipped capital femoral epiphysis because it better shows the posterior slippage of the femoral head.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the frog lateral view best demonstrates the subtle posterior displacement of the femoral head in mild slipped capital femoral epiphysis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because an anteroposterior view may miss subtle slips and is less sensitive for mild disease.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a skyline view is used for the patellofemoral joint, not the hip.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a weight-bearing standing view does not specifically improve detection of a mild slipped capital femoral epiphysis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a lateral decubitus view is not the standard view for diagnosing slipped capital femoral epiphysis.

source.hint: Think of the view that would best show the femoral head sliding 'posteriorly'.
